title: Foreign Currency Transactions and Translation - ASC 830

key_concepts.functional_currency: Currency of primary economic environment where entity operates (usually generates/spends cash)
key_concepts.reporting_currency: Currency in which entity prepares financial statements (USD for US companies)
key_concepts.foreign_currency_transaction: Transaction denominated in currency other than entity's functional currency

foreign_currency_transactions.definition: Transaction whose terms are denominated in foreign currency
accounting_process: 1. Initial recording: Translate at spot rate on transaction date
2. Balance sheet date: Remeasure monetary items at current rate, recognize G/L
3. Settlement date: Remeasure at spot rate, recognize G/L

foreign_exchange_gain_loss.recognition: In INCOME when exchange rates change between transaction date and settlement/balance sheet date
foreign_exchange_gain_loss.calculation: Foreign currency amount × (Current rate - Historical rate)

transaction_example.scenario: US company (USD functional currency) sells goods to German customer for €100,000 on Dec 1. Receives payment on Jan 15 next year.

accounting.entry:
DR Accounts Receivable $5,000
   CR Foreign Exchange Gain $5,000

DR Cash $122,000
DR Foreign Exchange Loss $3,000
   CR Accounts Receivable $125,000
accounting.net_effect: Net gain over whole period: $2,000 ($122K received - $120K sale)

indicators_of_functional_currency: Cash flows primarily in foreign currency
Sales prices responsive to local competition and regulation
Sales market primarily in foreign country

translation_method.when: Foreign currency IS functional currency (subsidiary relatively self-contained)
rates: Assets and liabilities: Current rate (balance sheet date)
Revenues and expenses: Average rate (or actual if material)
translation_method.translation_adjustment: Cumulative Translation Adjustment (CTA) in OCI (equity), NOT income
translation_method.purpose: Preserve relationships in foreign currency financial statements

remeasurement_method.when: USD IS functional currency (subsidiary extension of parent)
rates: Revenues and most expenses: Average rate
COGS, depreciation: Historical rates (related to historical cost assets)
remeasurement_method.purpose: Remeasure as if transactions occurred in USD

highly_inflationary_economies.accounting: Use remeasurement method (USD becomes functional currency)
highly_inflationary_economies.rationale: Foreign currency loses relevance in hyperinflation

cpa_exam_strategies.transaction_fx: Monetary items remeasured at current rate. Gain/loss in INCOME. Track AR/AP from transaction date through settlement.
cpa_exam_strategies.translation_vs_remeasurement: Translation (foreign functional): All at current rate except equity, differences in OCI. Remeasurement (USD functional): Monetary current, nonmonetary historical, differences in income.
cpa_exam_strategies.common_tested: Import/export transactions with FX gain/loss calculation. Translation vs. remeasurement distinction.

key_points: Foreign currency transactions: Monetary items remeasured at current rate, G/L in income
Initial recording at spot rate on transaction date
Remeasure at balance sheet date and settlement date
Foreign subsidiaries: Determine functional currency first
Translation (foreign functional): Current rate method, CTA in OCI
Remeasurement (USD functional): Monetary current / nonmonetary historical, G/L in income
Highly inflationary (≥100% over 3 years): Remeasurement required
